title: West Launch Lake Vista
description: Open view across the main basin from the west boat launch, with the north arm stretching away to the left and the dam far to the southeast.
alertText: Look left — the lake opens up beyond the launch

title: Marsh Creek Dam Overlook
description: The 90-foot-high, 990-foot-long earth-and-rock fill dam closes the south end of the lake. The dam was built between 1970 and 1973.
alertText: Ahead — the 990-foot dam holding back 535 acres of water

title: North Arm Overlook
description: The reservoir narrows into a winding north arm here, with drowned timber and quiet backwater habitat toward Little Conestoga Road.
alertText: Look left — the north arm winds away toward the woods

title: East Launch Marina View
description: Sailboats, rental craft and seasonal mooring slips fill the east basin beside the boat rental and snack bar.
alertText: Marina ahead — watch for sailboats crossing the basin

title: Milford Mills Ruins
description: Stone foundations and cellar holes mark the village of Milford Mills, the only settlement inside the area flooded for the reservoir.
alertText: Historic stone foundations on your left — Milford Mills

title: Murphy Mansion Site
description: Mike Murphy's 168-acre racehorse estate, including a 44-room mansion, once formed almost the whole village. The buildings were demolished during park development.
alertText: Murphy Mansion site — a 44-room house stood here

title: Larkin Covered Bridge Site
description: An 1854 covered bridge once spanned Marsh Creek at Milford Mills. It was moved to an Upper Uwchlan Township trail before the valley was flooded.
alertText: The 1854 Larkin covered bridge once crossed here

title: Dam Construction Interpretive Site
description: Construction ran from May 1970 to June 1973. The gates closed on November 16, 1973, and the lake reached normal pool on June 21, 1974.
alertText: 1970s dam works — the gates closed in November 1973

title: Heron Rookery
description: Drowned snags in the quiet north arm give herons and other wading birds a sheltered nesting and feeding area in spring.
alertText: Heron rookery on the north arm — quiet please

title: Osprey Platform
description: Ospreys are regular spring and fall migrants over the lake and rebuild stick nests on platform poles near the east shore.
alertText: Osprey platform ahead — look up and scan the sky

title: Bald Eagle Perch
description: Bald eagles patrol the open water here, especially in winter when migrating waterfowl concentrate on the lake.
alertText: Bald eagle often perches in the tall oak on the point

title: Turtle Basking Platforms
description: The lake's artificial fish-habitat program includes turtle basking platforms; painted and snapping turtles haul out on warm afternoons.
alertText: Count the turtles on the basking platforms

title: Grassland Bird Meadow
description: Warm-season grasses of Indian grass, big and little bluestem and switchgrass shelter bobolinks, meadowlarks, savannah sparrows and northern harriers.
alertText: Listen — bobolinks and meadowlarks nest in this grass

title: Wood Duck Cove
description: A sheltered cove off the east basin where wood ducks, mallards and spring migrants loaf in the flooded brush.
alertText: Quiet cove on the right — wood ducks frequent the brush

title: Dam Spillway
description: The concrete spillway carries releases around the earth-fill dam into Marsh Creek and the East Branch Brandywine downstream.

title: East Branch Brandywine
description: The East Branch of the Brandywine Creek threads the western woods and feeds the reservoir; the Blue Trail follows its bank.
alertText: Creek crossing ahead — the East Branch of the Brandywine

title: ADA Fishing Pier
description: The accessible fishing pier at the East Launch has ADA parking nearby and is the destination of the paved Park Road Trail.
alertText: Accessible fishing pier ahead — level paved approach

title: Sunset Point
description: A west-shore opening with an unobstructed sightline down the lake toward the dam — the park's classic evening photograph.
alertText: Sunset Point — arrive 30 minutes before dusk

title: North Arm Boardwalk
description: The widest boardwalk section on the accessible loop, with knee-high railings, passing bays and two benches looking down the north arm.
alertText: Boardwalk ahead — benches and open water on both sides
